summary: The author opened a new conversation and asked the model to check access to the repository and pick up handover 11.
verbatim: Please check if you have access to c:\git\business-intelligence and then look for Handover_11 in the handovers folder. Let's take if from there.

summary: Ran handover 11's first actions: tree clean, HEAD 7387aac equal to origin/main (S10 pushed); check_repo.py on a cloud copy passes apart from the 7 known logo errors (10 sessions, 70 register rows, 33 ADRs); read 142, ADR-0032, 147 to 149, ADR-0027 to ADR-0033, ARC-OP-29; sandbox status at simulated date 2016-06-02 with 15.41 GB free; opened S11.

Proposed the declaration format to the author in seven numbered points: model/ folder, the analysis record's flat grammar, permanent ids, only decisions declared, audit/status/effectivity satellites and types generated by rule, a coverage check of every source column, and a viewer with a hand-written force layout; flagged items 1, 2 and 7 as his choices.

blocker.detail: the author's reaction to the seven points, items 1, 2 and 7 in particular

summary: Wrote transcribe_wwi.py and transcribed the ruled tables of 147 to 149 into 124 declaration files under model/ (22 hubs, 49 links, 45 satellites, 7 reference tables, the source); found that six line links have no event date for their effectivity start (declared unknown) and declared link 28 optional as 149 Rule 5 reads it.

Wrote model/README.md (the proposed format) and tools/model_lib.py, and extended check_repo.py with check_model: completeness, naming, ids, references, citations to claims, and coverage of all 368 source columns exactly once; its first run found two transcription errors, fixed; five planted defects were all caught.

Built the first schema viewer: build.py reads model/ and the catalogue evidence into one static page (216 raw-vault and 48 source tables, focus view with a hand-written force layout, collapsed satellites, details panel, lineage between layers); checked by screenshots at desktop and phone width and published as an artifact for the author.

sol reviewed model/README.md alone against four stated standards and failed it with five findings: implicit driving end makes key reuse fail the check, mappings indistinguishable from composite keys, single-part parent_key, completeness and effectivity start not per mapping, names reusable.

check.expected: a format a deterministic generator can use without guessing, with stable identity and mechanical coverage

summary: Applied the review: links declare both ends per mapping with the effectivity start on the from line, composite keys and parent keys joined by ' + ', extract per base table, names and aliases never reused, one disposition per column with the reuse it implies; regenerated the 124 files, five new planted defects caught; fixed the viewer's lineage of links (it named the schema, not the table).

The author ruled the format: model/ as a top-level folder, the grammar, no library for the viewer; and the two link questions: the six line links' effectivity start stays unknown, link 28 is optional.

summary: Recorded the rulings in ADR-0034, set ARC-OP-29 to RULED with what stays open, marked model/README.md ruled, regenerated the declarations so the seven affected links cite ADR-0034.
The author asked to build the viewer.
verbatim: let's try to build the viewer.

summary: Rebuilt the viewer from the author's repository on his desktop (4 seconds, byte-identical to the committed page) and opened the published copy for him.
The author asked whether the analysis, its record and the viewer are repeatable at a client with a spaghetti database.
verbatim: This looks great! And this process is repeatable, right? This is obviously based on a practice database, but if I go to a client, I can reuse this right? I now have a client with a spaghetti database, and this functionality would come very much in handy. So first the automated analysis or the raw source, writing it away and then being able to navigate through it.

summary: Answered in eleven points: what carries over (record, model, viewer, method), what is WWI-specific (extraction, scripts, inferred relations, raw-only viewer, scale), what to settle first (confidentiality, where it runs); asked four sizing questions.

The author answered: PostgreSQL, about 100 tables, foreign keys probably declared, confidentiality open but the client has its own Claude subscriptions; proposed splitting the repository into process, use cases and website, pulling nsdn into a separate client repository.
verbatim: It's postgres, about 100 tables, it should have declared foreign keys, the question if the metadata may leave the client's premises is open, but they have their own Claude subscriptions, so I was thinking of maybe splitting this repository were working on, because we now have three parts, which is anything related to the process, the use cases (wwi and the dutch companies) and the website is also in here. I suppose it would be better to split the repository into three (nsdn process, use cases, website) and maybe then pulling the nsdn repository at the client site and set up a separate repository their for their data environment. They have a large-ish production database and two sources that deliver daily extracts from systems.

summary: Counted the cross-references a three-way split would cut (56 links into WWI material, 70 out, WWI ADRs in the one sequence) and proposed option B: WWI stays as reference case, company material out, one repository per client with a pinned nsdn; asked three questions.
The author ruled option B and a tagged release in client repositories, asked how improvements should travel both ways, and asked the model to go ahead with the PostgreSQL pass.
verbatim: Okay, there is something to be said for including the WWI set as a reference case. It's open, and provides a lot of practical examples. So option B. I think we should indeed pull a tagged release into a client repository. If the repository is improved, what do you suggest we do? Occasionally have a summary written and read that back into the main repository? And sometimes the other way back, if there are improvements in my main repository? Not sure what you want to do with the Postgress pass, but sounds plausible, so please go ahead.

summary: Wrote the PostgreSQL catalogue pass: catalogue_postgres.sql (read-only catalogue queries to CSV through psql) and ingest_catalogue.py (stdlib, catalogue evidence per table in the WWI shape, named by content hash).

check.expected: the pass gives back the structure of WWI's 48 tables rebuilt in PostgreSQL from its catalogue evidence
check.observed: 48 tables, 557 columns, 48 keys, 98 foreign keys, 280 descriptions, a test view and trigger agree; first run exposed the timestamp(7) mapping, fixed in the test

summary: Wrote test_against_wwi.py and ran it on a local PostgreSQL 16: the pass reproduces the WWI structure; the produced record passes the analysis checker.

Gave the viewer a raw-source mode for any source without a model (--root, --source, --out), with views, the tables they read and their SQL, triggers and estimated rows; fixed the catalogue reader dropping those fields.
Recorded the rulings in ADR-0035 and opened PRC-OP-9 with the proposal for how improvements travel (release notes downstream, upstream notes without client material).

check.expected: catalogue only, safe on production, complete structure, versions 12 to 17 with ordinary privileges
check.observed: FAILS, five findings: columns hidden without SELECT, partition bounds, expression indexes, NULLS NOT DISTINCT, temporary schemas

summary: sol reviewed catalogue_postgres.sql alone and failed it with five findings.

Applied all five findings (column privilege filter removed, partition bounds, key expressions, nulls_not_distinct via to_jsonb, temporary schemas excluded everywhere) and extended the test to each: passes run as a login with no table privilege, for which the old filter returned 0 of 557 columns.
